primitives.verbatim_quote: The method as defined in claim 3, wherein the perfor mance data parameters include at least one of a physiological load, a mechanical load, a mechanical intensity, a physical intensity, a number of games played, average running seconds, average field goals, or previous injuries.

primitives.assumptions: Injury probability varies continuously with time and is modeled as a function of seasonal data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t approaches end of season, P_{injury}(t) may exceed 1 due to cumulative exposure.

primitives.name: Performance Similarity Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: The method as defined in claim 1, wherein the sum of similarity factors is a sum of percentages representative of amounts of similarity between performance data parameters of the second players and the target player.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_{sim}': 'Sum of similarity factors, dimensionless', 'p_i': 'Percentage similarity for parameter i, percent'}
primitives.assumptions: Similarity is additive across performance parameters and normalized to 100% maximum.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S_{sim} exceeds 100%, indicates overfitting or redundant features.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically maps performance vectors to similarity space for cohort selection.
layer2.telemetry: Average cosine similarity between target and peer performance vectors

primitives.name: Weighted Injury Likelihood
primitives.verbatim_quote: The apparatus as defined in claim 9, wherein the performance data parameters include at least one of a physiological load, a mechanical bad, a mechanical intensity, a physical intensity, a number of games played, average running seconds, average field goals, or previous injuries.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'W_{injury}': 'Weighted injury likelihood, dimensionless', 'L_{physio}': 'Physiological load, arbitrary units', 'I_{prev}': 'Previous injuries count, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Weighted likelihood is linear combination of load and injury history with learned coefficients.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When L_{physio} becomes extremely high, W_{injury} may saturate or diverge.

layer2.mapping: Derives injury risk from weighted performance parameters using regression coefficients.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized score of injury risk from peer-weighted parameters

reasoning_traces.think:
The framework integrates three core components: temporal injury modeling, performance similarity indexing, and weighted injury likelihood estimation. Temporal models assume continuous variation of injury risk with time, grounded in observed seasonality. Performance similarity is computed as a sum of normalized percentage matches across key biomechanical and physiological parameters. Weighted injury likelihood combines these with historical injury counts and load metrics. Dualities emerge in how temporal data informs similarity thresholds and vice versa—seasonal trends can modulate what constitutes a 'similar' athlete. Failure modes include overfitting when too many parameters are used without regularization, or misalignment between similarity indices and actual injury outcomes due to unmodeled confounders such as recovery protocols or environmental stressors.
